records.source: בְּ֭נִי לְחָכְמָתִ֣י הַקְשִׁ֑יבָה לִ֝תְבוּנָתִ֗י הַט־אָזְנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: My son, to my wisdom pay attention; to my understanding incline your ear,
pieces: My son, listen closely to the wisdom I have; \q bend your ear to what I understand,

L.1: My son, to my wisdom pay attention; \q to my understanding incline your ear,

R.1: My son, pay attention to my wise teaching. \q Listen carefully to what I understand.

decisions.choice: my wisdom ... my understanding: what the father has learned
decisions.reason: The father speaks of wisdom he has gained by living, as in 4:3–4.

records.heading: The bitter end of adultery

records.source: לִשְׁמֹ֥ר מְזִמּ֑וֹת וְ֝דַ֗עַת שְׂפָתֶ֥יךָ יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: to keep discretion, and knowledge your lips will guard.
pieces: so that you keep your foresight \q and your lips guard what you know.

L.2: to keep discretion, \q and your lips will guard knowledge.

R.2: Then you will make wise choices, \q and you will say what is true and wise.

decisions.choice: discretion: foresight, thinking ahead
decisions.reason: The word (mezimmah, here plural) is the one in 1:4 and 2:11. The son will need it against the smooth lips of verse 3.

decisions.choice: your lips: what you say
decisions.reason: His lips are set against hers (verse 3): his words keep knowledge, hers drip honey.

records.source: כִּ֤י נֹ֣פֶת תִּ֭טֹּפְנָה שִׂפְתֵ֣י זָרָ֑ה וְחָלָ֖ק מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן חִכָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: For honey drip [the] lips of a strange [woman], and smoother than oil [is] her palate,
pieces: For honey drips from the lips of the woman who is not yours, \q and her talk is smoother than olive oil,

L.3: For the lips of a strange [woman] drip honey, \q and her palate [is] smoother than oil,

R.3: A woman who belongs to another man may say sweet things. \q Her words may seem smooth and pleasant.

decisions.choice: a strange woman: a woman who is not his to have
decisions.reason: The word (zarah) is the one in 2:16. Verses 15–20 set her against the son's own wife.

decisions.choice: honey ... smoother than oil: sweet, flattering talk
decisions.reason: Her palate (hek) stands for her speech (8:7), as in 2:16 and 7:21. The lips may also suggest her kisses (Song of Songs 4:11).

decisions.choice: the woman who is not yours
decisions.reason: As in 2:16, Balanced says what makes her "strange": she is not his to have.

records.source: וְֽ֭אַחֲרִיתָהּ מָרָ֣ה כַֽלַּעֲנָ֑ה חַ֝דָּ֗ה כְּחֶ֣רֶב פִּיּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: but her end [is] bitter like wormwood, sharp like a sword of mouths.
pieces: but what she leaves you with is bitter as wormwood, \q and it cuts like a two-edged sword.

L.4: but her end [is] bitter as wormwood, \q sharp as a two-edged sword.

R.4: But in the end, she brings bitter pain. \q She cuts like a sharp sword.

decisions.choice: wormwood: a bitter plant
decisions.reason: Wormwood (laanah) is a plant with a very bitter taste, used as a picture of bitter suffering (Lamentations 3:15; Amos 5:7).

decisions.choice: a sword of mouths: a two-edged sword
decisions.reason: A sword's edges are called its "mouths" because they "eat" (Judges 3:16).

decisions.choice: her end: what she leads to in the end
decisions.reason: "Her end" is the outcome of going with her, set against the sweetness at the start (verse 3; 14:12).

records.source: רַ֭גְלֶיהָ יֹרְד֣וֹת מָ֑וֶת שְׁ֝א֗וֹל צְעָדֶ֥יהָ יִתְמֹֽכוּ׃
records.gloss: Her feet [are] going down [to] death; [to] Sheol her steps take hold.
pieces: Her feet go down toward death; \q her steps make straight for Sheol.

L.5: Her feet go down [to] death; \q her steps take hold [of] Sheol.

R.5: The road she walks leads down to death and the grave.

decisions.choice: her steps take hold of Sheol: they lead straight there
decisions.reason: Her steps "grasp" Sheol, the place of the dead (1:12): they go nowhere else (2:18; 7:27).

decisions.choice: Sheol
decisions.reason: As in 1:12, Literal and Balanced keep the name; Readable says "the grave".

records.source: אֹ֣רַח חַ֭יִּים פֶּן־תְּפַלֵּ֑ס נָע֥וּ מַ֝עְגְּלֹתֶ֗יהָ לֹ֣א תֵדָֽע׃פ
records.gloss: [The] path of life lest she weigh, her tracks wander; she does not know.
pieces: She does not consider the road to life; \q her ways drift, and she is unaware of it.

L.6: She does not weigh [the] path of life; \q her tracks wander, [and] she does not know [it].

R.6: She does not care about living the right way. \q She wanders without knowing where she is going.

decisions.choice: she does not weigh the path of life
alternatives: so that you do not weigh the path of life
lest she find the path of life
decisions.reason: The line is hard. The verbs can be read as "she" or "you", and the first word (pen) means "lest". Most likely it says that she never stops to think where her road leads, so it wanders. Others read it as a warning to the son: she keeps you from thinking about the path of life.

decisions.choice: weigh: think out, make level
decisions.reason: The verb (pilles) of 4:26, where the son is told to make his own path level.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־לִ֑י וְאַל־תָּ֝ס֗וּרוּ מֵאִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃
records.gloss: And now, sons, listen to me, and do not turn aside from [the] sayings of my mouth.
pieces: So now, sons, hear me out, \q and do not stray from the words I speak.

L.7: And now, sons, listen to me, \q and do not turn aside from [the] sayings of my mouth.

R.7: So, sons, listen to me. \q Keep on doing what I tell you.

decisions.choice: sons: the plural address of 4:1
decisions.reason: The father turns to his sons in the plural, then back to the singular "you" in verse 8.

records.heading: Keep away from her door

records.source: הַרְחֵ֣ק מֵעָלֶ֣יהָ דַרְכֶּ֑ךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝קְרַ֗ב אֶל־פֶּ֥תַח בֵּיתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Make far from her your way, and do not draw near to [the] door of her house,
pieces: Keep well away from her, \q and do not even come near her front door,

L.8: Keep your way far from her, \q and do not draw near to [the] door of her house,

R.8: Stay far away from her. \q Do not even go near the door of her house.

decisions.choice: the door of her house: where temptation is met
decisions.reason: Chapter 7 tells of a young man who walks by her corner and is drawn in at her door (7:8, 27). The father's advice is distance.

records.source: פֶּן־תִּתֵּ֣ן לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים הוֹדֶ֑ךָ וּ֝שְׁנֹתֶ֗יךָ לְאַכְזָרִֽי׃
records.gloss: lest you give to others your splendor, and your years to a cruel [one],
pieces: or you will hand over your strength to others \q and your years to someone without mercy,

L.9: lest you give your splendor to others, \q and your years to a cruel [one],

R.9: If you do, other people will take your strength, \q and a cruel person will take the best years of your life.

decisions.choice: splendor: vigor, the best of a man's strength
decisions.reason: The word (hod) means majesty or splendor (Psalm 45:4). Here it is the vigor and dignity of a man's life, spent on others.

decisions.choice: a cruel one: someone who will show no mercy
decisions.reason: The verse does not say who it is. It may be the woman's husband, who will take revenge (6:34–35), or anyone who takes advantage of a man caught in adultery.

records.source: פֶּֽן־יִשְׂבְּע֣וּ זָרִ֣ים כֹּחֶ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲצָבֶ֗יךָ בְּבֵ֣ית נָכְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: lest strangers be sated [with] your strength, and your toils [be] in [the] house of a foreigner,
pieces: and strangers will feed on your wealth, \q and what you worked hard for will end up in an outsider's house,

L.10: lest strangers be filled [with] your strength, \q and your toils [go] to [the] house of a foreigner,

R.10: Strangers will enjoy your money, \q and what you worked for will belong to someone else's family.

decisions.choice: your strength: your wealth, the product of your strength
decisions.reason: The word (koah) is strength, and also what strength earns (Job 6:22).

decisions.choice: strangers ... a foreigner: outsiders
decisions.reason: The same two words used of the woman in 2:16 and 5:20. Her world takes what was his.

records.source: וְנָהַמְתָּ֥ בְאַחֲרִיתֶ֑ךָ בִּכְל֥וֹת בְּ֝שָׂרְךָ֗ וּשְׁאֵרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: and you will groan at your end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,
pieces: and when it is all over you will groan, \q your body wasted and your flesh used up,

L.11: and you will groan at your end, \q when your flesh and your body are consumed,

R.11: At the end, your body will be worn out, \q and you will cry in pain.

decisions.choice: groan: moan in distress
decisions.reason: The verb (naham) is used of a lion's growl (19:12) and of the moaning of the suffering (Ezekiel 24:23).

decisions.choice: your flesh and your body are consumed: worn out
decisions.reason: The verse does not say how: by disease, by poverty, or simply by a life spent badly. It is the bitter end of verse 4.

records.source: וְֽאָמַרְתָּ֗ אֵ֭יךְ שָׂנֵ֣אתִי מוּסָ֑ר וְ֝תוֹכַ֗חַת נָאַ֥ץ לִבִּֽי׃
records.gloss: and you will say, How I hated discipline, and rebuke my heart despised,
pieces: and you will say, "How I hated being corrected! \q How my heart despised every warning!

L.12: and you will say, "How I hated discipline, \q and my heart despised rebuke!

R.12: Then you will say, "Why did I hate it when people corrected me? \q Why did I refuse to listen to warnings?

decisions.choice: you will say: the son's regret, running to the end of verse 14
decisions.reason: The father puts into the son's mouth the words he would say too late (1:24–31).

records.source: וְֽלֹא־שָׁ֭מַעְתִּי בְּק֣וֹל מוֹרָ֑י וְ֝לִֽמְלַמְּדַ֗י לֹא־הִטִּ֥יתִי אָזְנִֽי׃
records.gloss: and I did not listen to [the] voice of my teachers, and to my instructors I did not incline my ear.
pieces: I paid no attention to what my teachers said; \q I would not lend an ear to those who taught me.

L.13: I did not listen to [the] voice of my teachers, \q and to my instructors I did not incline my ear.

R.13: I did not listen to my teachers. \q I did not pay attention to the people who taught me.

decisions.choice: teachers ... instructors: the father and others who taught
decisions.reason: The first word (moreh) is from the root of torah, teaching (4:2, 11). The father counts himself among them.

records.source: כִּ֭מְעַט הָיִ֣יתִי בְכָל־רָ֑ע בְּת֖וֹךְ קָהָ֣ל וְעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: Almost I was in every evil in [the] midst of [the] assembly and congregation.
pieces: I came close to complete ruin, \q there in front of the whole assembled community."

L.14: Almost I was in every evil, \q in [the] midst of [the] assembly and congregation."

R.14: Now I am almost completely ruined, \q and everyone knows it."

decisions.choice: almost in every evil: close to complete ruin
alternatives: in a moment I was in great trouble
decisions.reason: The phrase (kimat) can mean "almost" or "in a moment". Either way he has come to ruin.

decisions.choice: the assembly and congregation: the community, gathered for judgment
decisions.reason: The two words name the people of Israel gathered together. Adultery could be judged in public (Deuteronomy 22:22; 6:33), so his ruin is public shame, and may be a legal penalty.

records.source: שְׁתֵה־מַ֥יִם מִבּוֹרֶ֑ךָ וְ֝נֹזְלִ֗ים מִתּ֥וֹךְ בְּאֵרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Drink water from your cistern, and flowing [water] from [the] midst of your well.
pieces: Draw your water from your own cistern, \q the fresh streams from inside your own well.

L.15: Drink water from your [own] cistern, \q and flowing [water] from [the] midst of your [own] well.

R.15: Be faithful to your own wife and enjoy her love, \q like a man who drinks water from his own well.

decisions.choice: drink water from your own cistern: find love with your own wife
decisions.reason: In a dry land, a cistern or well of one's own was precious. The Song of Songs uses the same pictures of a bride (Song of Songs 4:12, 15). Verse 18 names her: "the wife of your youth".

decisions.choice: Be faithful to your own wife
alternatives: Drink water from your own cistern
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1) and keeps it as a comparison.

records.source: יָפ֣וּצוּ מַעְיְנֹתֶ֣יךָ ח֑וּצָה בָּ֝רְחֹב֗וֹת פַּלְגֵי־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Should your springs overflow outside, in the squares streams of water?
pieces: Why let your springs run out into the street, \q and your streams flow through the town squares?

L.16: Should your springs overflow outside, \q streams of water in the squares?

R.16: Why waste your love on other women, \q like water spilling into the street?

decisions.choice: should your springs overflow outside? a question expecting "no"
alternatives: Let your springs flow outside (a statement)
decisions.reason: Hebrew does not always mark a question. Read as a question, the verse warns against wasting the son's love on other women, and verse 17 follows: "let them be yours alone". Some read it as a promise of children; others as the wife's love flowing to others if he is unfaithful.

records.source: יִֽהְיוּ־לְךָ֥ לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֖ין לְזָרִ֣ים אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Let them be to you alone, and not to strangers with you.
pieces: Keep them for yourself alone, \q with no strangers drinking beside you.

L.17: Let them be for you alone, \q and not for strangers with you.

R.17: Your love should be for you and your wife alone, \q not for anyone else.

decisions.choice: strangers: outsiders
decisions.reason: The word (zarim) is the one used of the strange woman (5:3, 20) and of those who take his strength (5:10).

records.source: יְהִֽי־מְקוֹרְךָ֥ בָר֑וּךְ וּ֝שְׂמַ֗ח מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת נְעוּרֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: May your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in [the] wife of your youth,
pieces: May your spring be blessed; \q find your joy in the woman you married when you were young,

L.18: Let your fountain be blessed, \q and rejoice in [the] wife of your youth,

R.18: May God bless your marriage. \q Be happy with the woman you married when you were young.

decisions.choice: blessed: blessed by God
decisions.reason: This word (baruk) is used of what God blesses, unlike "how blessed" (ashre) in 3:13. The fountain is his wife, and the blessing may include children.

decisions.choice: the wife of your youth: the wife he married when young
decisions.reason: The phrase looks back to the start of the marriage (2:17; Malachi 2:14–15).

decisions.choice: May God bless your marriage
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the one who blesses (m1), and says what the fountain stands for.

records.source: אַיֶּ֥לֶת אֲהָבִ֗ים וְֽיַעֲלַ֫ת־חֵ֥ן דַּ֭דֶּיהָ יְרַוֻּ֣ךָ בְכָל־עֵ֑ת בְּ֝אַהֲבָתָ֗הּ תִּשְׁגֶּ֥ה תָמִֽיד׃
records.gloss: a doe of love and a mountain goat of grace; her breasts, may they satisfy you at every time; by her love may you be intoxicated continually.
pieces: a lovely doe, a graceful mountain goat. \q Let her breasts content you at every season, \q and let her love carry you away always.

L.19: a doe of love and a mountain goat of grace; \q let her breasts satisfy you at all times; \q by her love be intoxicated continually.

R.19: She is beautiful and lovely, like a young deer. \q Let her body always satisfy you. \q Let her love fill you with joy.

decisions.choice: a doe ... a mountain goat: pictures of a woman's beauty
decisions.reason: The doe and the wild goat were known for their grace and beauty. The Song of Songs uses such animals in its love poetry (Song of Songs 2:9; 4:5).

decisions.choice: be intoxicated: be carried away, as if drunk
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) means to reel or stagger, and so to go astray. The father uses it three times: be carried away by your wife's love (verse 19), not by another woman (verse 20), or you will be carried away to death by your folly (verse 23).

decisions.choice: carry you away
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same English verb in verses 19, 20 and 23, so the reader can see the wordplay (m2).

records.source: וְלָ֤מָּה תִשְׁגֶּ֣ה בְנִ֣י בְזָרָ֑ה וּ֝תְחַבֵּ֗ק חֵ֣ק נָכְרִיָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And why should you be intoxicated, my son, with a strange [woman], and embrace [the] bosom of a foreign [woman]?
pieces: Why, my son, let yourself be carried away by a woman who is not yours, \q or take an outsider in your arms?

L.20: Why should you be intoxicated, my son, with a strange [woman], \q and embrace [the] bosom of a foreign [woman]?

R.20: My son, why let another man's wife excite you? \q Why hold her in your arms?

decisions.choice: a strange woman ... a foreign woman: as in 2:16
decisions.reason: The same pair of words as in 2:16; the father has come back to where the chapter began (verse 3).

records.source: כִּ֤י נֹ֨כַח׀עֵינֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה דַּרְכֵי־אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל־מַעְגְּלֹתָ֥יו מְפַלֵּֽס׃
records.gloss: For before [the] eyes of YHWH [are the] ways of a man, and all his tracks he weighs.
pieces: For everything a person does is in plain view of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} weighs every path they take.

L.21: For before [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [are the] ways of {{gender:a person|a man}}, \q and all {{gender:their|his}} tracks {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} weighs.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sees everything people do. \q He watches every step they take.

decisions.choice: weighs: examines, or makes level
decisions.reason: The verb (pilles) of 4:26 and 5:6. The LORD looks over every road a person takes, so nothing done in secret is hidden from him (15:3; Job 31:4).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone
decisions.reason: The word (ish) here means any person, though the warning is to the son.

records.source: עַֽווֹנוֹתָ֗יויִלְכְּדֻנ֥וֹ אֶת־הָרָשָׁ֑ע וּבְחַבְלֵ֥י חַ֝טָּאת֗וֹ יִתָּמֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: His iniquities will capture him, the wicked, and in [the] cords of his sin he will be held.
pieces: Their own wrongdoing will catch the wicked, \q and the ropes of their sin will tie them up.

L.22: {{gender:Their|His}} iniquities will capture the wicked, \q and in [the] cords of {{gender:their|his}} sin {{gender:they|he}} will be held.

R.22: Evil people get trapped by the bad things they do. \q Their sins are like ropes that tie them up.

decisions.choice: capture ... cords: sin is a trap the sinner sets for himself
decisions.reason: The picture is of a hunter's snare. The wicked need no one else to catch them (1:18; Psalm 7:16–17).

records.source: ה֗וּא יָ֭מוּת בְּאֵ֣ין מוּסָ֑ר וּבְרֹ֖ב אִוַּלְתּ֣וֹ יִשְׁגֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: He will die for lack of discipline, and in [the] greatness of his folly he will go astray.
pieces: Such people die for lack of discipline, \q carried away by their great folly.

L.23: {{gender:They|He}} will die for lack of discipline, \q and in [the] greatness of {{gender:their|his}} folly {{gender:they|he}} will stagger.

R.23: They will die because they would not accept correction. \q Their great foolishness will lead them away.

decisions.choice: stagger: be carried away, go astray
decisions.reason: The verb (shagah) of verses 19–20. The man who was carried away by a strange woman is now carried away to death.

decisions.choice: folly: the stubbornness of the fool
decisions.reason: The word (iwwelet) belongs to the fool of 1:7, who despises discipline.
